A little about me

Language is
where I begin.

My work connects computational linguistics with the practical questions of building and evaluating AI.

My research interests include linguistic typology, commonsense reasoning, phonetics, and Korean language resources. I earned my Ph.D. in Korean Linguistics at Kyung Hee University in August 2023.

At Lablup, I work as a researcher. Alongside research, I teach, write, and organize communities that help people explore language and technology together.

Learning, together

Inference Korea.

From understanding models
to running them well.

72Discord membersAs of October 2026

Inference Korea is a study community focused on inference engineering: how to run AI models efficiently and reliably. We learn through book discussions, research paper presentations, and shared exploration of inference engines.

01

Read & understand

Study Inference Engineering by Patrick Kiely, from inference fundamentals and GPU architecture to software and production deployment.

02

Discuss & connect

Members take turns presenting chapters and related papers, connecting ideas such as quantization, caching, model parallelism, and performance measurement.

03

Put it into practice

After the reading and discussion phase, we plan to continue with hands-on sessions to apply what we have learned about inference engines and model serving.

Our study plan
